Welcome to BeyondAutism Schools, where we are committed to empowering every pupil and where nothing is considered impossible.
Our fundamental belief is that every child and young adult has the potential to succeed and make a unique and significant contribution to society.
Each of our pupils is provided with a truly personalised curriculum and one-to-one support by dedicated and passionate staff using teaching strategies underpinned by the understanding of behaviour (behaviour analysis).
Through the promotion of a happy, caring environment our pupils and staff gain respect for each other, nurture confidence, independence and self-belief. You will see from our website the kind of work we do, and how our approach achieves the most positive outcomes for autistic children and young adults. However, it is only by paying us a visit that you can see the truly excellent provision we offer.
We hope that you find our website useful, and that you find the information you are looking for. Please feel free to contact us with any queries you may have.
Matthew Le Blanc Head of Park House School
Corey Bulmer Head of Tram House School

Vision, Aims and Values
Our vision is to ensure autistic children and young adults access an education which empowers a life full of choice, independence and opportunity.
We aim to achieve this by:
Our Values
At BeyondAutism we are:
Dedicated to delivering excellence
Developing expertise, outstanding services and positive engagement, always seeking to go above and beyond expectations.
Committed to Behaviour Analysis, underpinned by the science of Applied Behaviour Analysis and Verbal Behaviour
Contributing to research and ensuring our staff continually develop and share best practice that ensure aspirational outcomes are achieved for autistic individuals.
Embracing diversity, showing integrity, acting with compassion and always treating people with dignity.
Listening, changing thinking, shifting attitudes and educating.

About Us
BeyondAutism Schools run Park House School and Tram House School, Independent Special Schools for autistic children and young adults. In line with a federation-type model the schools have separate registrations with the DfE but sit under a single elected BeyondAutism Schools Governing Body.
Heads of School Matthew Le Blanc (Park House School) and Corey Bulmer (Tram House School) are supported by the Senior Leadership Teams, who are responsible for the teaching and learning in both schools; the achievement and progress of all pupils, the curriculum and the day to day running of the schools.
BeyondAutism Schools is a service run by the charity BeyondAutism.

Our History
BeyondAutism was founded as The Rainbow Charity in 2000, when a group of parents founded Rainbow School with 3 pupils in a run-down pre-fabricated hut on the grounds of Beatrix Potter School in Wandsworth.
Since then, the charity and school have undergone a remarkable transformation, growing exponentially in response to need. We now deliver transformative education to pupils from 19 Local Authorities across London.
Having purchased both school sites, our buildings were renovated specifically for our learners’ needs. In September 2017, Rainbow School became two separate schools, Park House School and Tram House School With Sixth Form numbers rising, in 2019 some of our Sixth Form pupils started to access space at South Thames College focusing on independent living skills. In 2022 the Sixth Form moved into a permanent home in Roehampton.
We are very proud of where we are today and look forward to the impact we can have for autistic individuals for decades to come.

Parents
BeyondAutism was founded by a dedicated, enthusiastic group of parents. Working in partnership with parents continues to be at the core of all our services and we strive to maintain positive relationships that benefit our pupils. Our schools actively seek engagement with all parents and respect that each family will have different needs at different times. Whilst there are formal channels of communication we also embrace an open door policy, inviting parents to visit, get involved with activities and to provide feedback.
Our parents also provide an important peer support network to each other with a dedicated Facebook group which is open to all parents of pupils at a BeyondAutism School. All parents are required to follow a code of conduct for use.

Governing Body and Trustees
Our Governors
Our Governing Body meets every half term (six times a year) and works across both Park House School and Tram House School. Governors attend at least one full training day a year.
Our Governors are actively involved in many aspects of school life and are completely committed to the success of the school and to ensuring the best possible provision for our pupils.
Governors are recruited from across the school community including parents, staff and members of the local community. Parent Governors are elected by the parents. Staff Governors are elected by the staff, and staff from across the schools are encouraged to stand.
Governing Body Composition
Staff/Behaviour Analyist
Tracie Coultas-Pitman
Head of Park House School
Head of Tram House School
If you would like to get in touch with the Governing Body, you can contact the clerk here.
For more information on how we govern our schools, you can read:
How We Govern Our Schools
Our Trustees
Park House School and Tram House School are run by BeyondAutism, a registered charity. The charity provides education, outreach, training and support for autistic children and young adults, their families and the professionals that work with them.
BeyondAutism is governed by a Board of Trustees consisting of individuals who contribute a wide range of expertise and experience to the charity. Angus Johnston is the current Chair of Trustees. The Board meet four times a year and are responsible for strategic development and ensuring the smooth running of the charity.
BeyondAutism is committed to ensuring that it offers equality of opportunity in its governance, service provision and employment practice.
Getting in touch with our Board of Trustees
If you’d like to reach our Trustees, you can do so by writing to:
The Board of Trustees Gatehouse by Spacemade, 1 Armoury Way, London, SW18 1TH
Or by calling 020 3031 9705.

Our Team
Park House School Senior Leadership Team
Matthew Le Blanc
Head of Park House School
Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead
Matthew Le Blanc commenced his career at BeyondAutism in 2013, following the completion of his undergraduate degree in Psychology with Neuroscience. He began as a Teaching and Learning Practitioner, where he quickly developed a strong commitment to Behaviour Analysis, inspired by its demonstrable impact on pupil outcomes. Over the years, Matthew progressed through several roles within the organisation, before pursuing formal teacher training.
He completed his teacher training at the Institute of Education and continued his professional journey at BeyondAutism as a Qualified Teacher, whilst studying Applied Behavioural Analysis MSC at the University of Belfast. In September 2022, he was appointed Head of Park House School.
Matthew is deeply committed to fostering pupil independence and ensuring that functional skills acquired in the classroom are effectively transferred to everyday life.
Catrin Bail
Deputy Head of Park House
Designated Safeguarding Lead
Catrin graduated from the University of Kent with a degree in Psychology. During her time at university she embarked on various work and volunteer placements with children and young people with special needs, specifically autism.
Catrin joined BeyondAutism as an ABA Tutor in 2015. She undertook her teacher training and became a Qualified Teacher in 2019. Catrin is now working at Park House School in the role of Pastoral Lead.
Catrin is passionate about supporting learners and their families to achieve the best outcomes and promoting positive mental health and wellbeing.
Chloe Watkins
Head of Therapy Services
Chloe has a strong history with BeyondAutism, having originally joined the charity in 2000, as an ABA Tutor. She completed an undergraduate degree in Psychology and Education before qualifying as a Speech and Language Therapist in 2004. Chloe has worked with children and young people, in a range of clinical, mainstream and specialist settings, specialising in Social Communication.
Chloe is excited to be Head of Therapy Services, working with an exceptional team. She is passionate about supporting individuals to develop the functional communication and independence skills, that enable them to confidently access and enjoy everyday activities.
Karen Talty
Consultant Behaviour Analyst
Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead
Karen studied her Masters in ABA in Ireland before moving to London over 11 years ago. She has worked in various ABA settings across Greater London including Jigsaw School, Ambitious College, Snowflake School as well as for Hillingdon Local Authority.
Karen has worked with a range of individuals with autism from the age of 4 through to 21. She has been Board Certified for since 2016 and is enjoying working with BeyondAutism immensely. Karen has provided training to staff, parents, mainstream and special schools and wider professionals in Behaviour Analysis.
Karen has a passion for teaching communication skills in particular and researching new techniques for enabling our learners to live a more independent life.
Jess Hargreaves
Occupational Therapist
Jess has always enjoyed working in paediatric OT and is passionate about supporting pupils to achieve their potential! She has been fortunate enough to work in schools that specialise in working with children and young people with autism for most of her career but she also has experience in a NHS community paediatrics role. This was invaluable as it gave her a broad understanding of many conditions and challenges that people may be facing in a variety of settings. She is now able to combine all of her experience to look at each pupil as an individual to provide holistic Occupational Therapy input.
Tram House School Senior Leadership Team
Corey Bulmer
Interim Head of Tram House Secondary
Head of Pastoral Tram House
With over 10 years of experience in both SEN and mainstream education, Corey began his career teaching Fashion & Textiles in further education before transitioning to SEN. Corey served as a Curriculum & Therapy Lead in a SEN college and recently as Head of Centre for a new SEMH provision, which he helped to establish.
Corey is dedicated to ensuring that all young people have access to an enriching curriculum that promotes independence and aligns with their future aspirations. He believes that education should be nurturing, inclusive of student voices, and tailored to individual needs. Upon joining BeyondAutism, he is most excited about collaborating with young people, their families, and other agencies to support their growth and success.
Bobbie Stone
Assistant Head of Tram House Secondary
Bobbie joined BeyondAutism in 2018 and has progressed from Behaviour Analyst to Consultant Behaviour Analyst, and now Assistant Head of Tram House School and Sixth Form. Since beginning her Behaviour Analysis career in 2012, she has supported autistic young people aged 3–21 across home, school, and NHS settings.
In 2023, she completed a Postgraduate Diploma in Improving Access to Psychological Therapies (IAPT) for autistic children and those with learning disabilities, strengthening her multidisciplinary practice.
Passionate about neurodiversity?affirming approaches, Bobbie works closely with families and professionals to create meaningful, strengths?based learning experiences that help young people feel understood, celebrated, and empowered.
Jordana Smallwood
MSc, BSc, BCBA, QTLS
Head of Tram House Sixth Form
Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead
Jordana's dedicated career in behaviour analysis began with hands-on work in ABA home programs, leading her to BeyondAutism in 2012 after earning her Psychology degree. Starting as an ABA Tutor, she rapidly advanced through roles including Class Leader and ABA Supervisor, culminating in her current leadership position as Head of Tram House Sixth Form. In this role, she is deeply committed to preparing pupils for adulthood, focusing on holistic growth that equips them with the skills and confidence for life beyond school.
A graduate of Bangor University with a Master's in Applied Behaviour Analysis, Jordana became a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) in 2018 and has recently achieved Qualified Teacher Learning and Skills (QTLS) status. Her passion lies in creating engaging learning environments, where she thrives on witnessing pupils joyfully acquire new skills and develop the independence necessary for their futures.
Chloe Watkins
Head of Therapy Services
Chloe has a strong history with BeyondAutism, having originally joined the charity in 2000, as an ABA Tutor. She completed an undergraduate degree in Psychology and Education before qualifying as a Speech and Language Therapist in 2004. Chloe has worked with children and young people, in a range of clinical, mainstream and specialist settings, specialising in Social Communication.
Chloe is excited to be Head of Therapy Services, working with an exceptional team. She is passionate about supporting individuals to develop the functional communication and independence skills, that enable them to confidently access and enjoy everyday activities.
Melissa Fernandes
Consultant Behaviour Analyst Sixth Form
Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead
MSc in Health Psychology; BSc Hons in Psychology; PG Dip with Distinction Applied Behaviour Analysis
Melissa began work at BeyondAutism Schools as a Trainee ABA Tutor, being promoted to Class Leader after 3 years. During this time she completed a Masters in Health Psychology, which led her to a role in the health sector involving behaviour change, outreach and health awareness and promotion.
In 2015 Melissa decided to return to the field of Behaviour Analysis as a home Tutor, while completing a Postgraduate Diploma in Applied Behaviour Analysis. She started gaining supervision hours by overseeing home programmes that enabled her to return to BeyondAutism as a Behaviour Analyst this year. She hopes this role will further her knowledge, continue to grow her professional development and allow her to apply her insights from the home setting in the schools. Melissa is a qualified BCBA.
Chelsee Maloney
Consultant Behaviour Analyst
Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead
Chelsee studied English Language and Literature at Queen Mary University London, intending to become an English teacher. After gaining experience in mainstream settings, supporting pupils with additional needs in a secondary school, Chelsee's ambition changed, and she began looking for a specialist role in the Special Educational Needs sector. This led Chelsee to BeyondAutism and she has not looked back since.
Chelsee joined BeyondAutism in September 2016 and has worked in a multitude of roles during her time here, following the pathway from Teaching and Learning Practitioner up to Behaviour Analyst. After 5 years as a Behaviour Analyst, Chelsee is now the Consultant Behaviour Analyst at Tram House School.
Chelsee completed a MSc in Applied Behaviour Analysis and is a BCBA and UK-BA Cert. Chelsee's focus is ensuring trauma-informed practice is embedded across Tram House School.
Abigail Darko
Occupational Therapist
Abigail is an experienced Occupational Therapist and joined BeyondAutism in January 2024.
Previously she worked for an outer London local authority within the Transitions/Preparing for adulthood team. The role involved supporting young adults with SEND, mental health and care leavers to live fulfilling independent lives through skill development, coaching and empowerment. Abi is passionate about supporting young people, especially with additional needs, to thrive in whatever it is they want or need to do.
Administrators
Bhavini Chotai
Bhavini joined BeyondAutism in 2021. She has always tailored her education and career around working with children and young people with autism and special needs. She began working with children and young people with special needs when she was in Canada. After moving to UK she continued on this career path and has come to BeyondAutism from Treehouse school where she was a Teaching and Behaviour Support before moving to admissions and administration.
She feels happy when she is able to place children and young people in education and being part of providing them access to education that they deserve. She is excited to bring her wealth of knowledge and experience to the organisation. To work in a motivating environment and be part of the BeyondAutism team will be amazing.
Jamila Skeete

Curriculum
Pupils in the Sixth Form follow individualised programmes that respond to individual needs. The personalised timetables are built around the pupil’s Individual Education Plan and Education, Health and Care Plan. For our Post-16 pupils, their outcomes are built around the Preparing for Adulthood strands: health and wellbeing, independent living, community participation and vocational and employment. They receive group teaching in the following subject areas: literacy, numeracy, STEM, PSHE, computing, physical education and performing arts.
Pupils in the Sixth Form have an opportunity to engage in a wide range of physical and mental health activities, including: accessing the gym, yoga, P.E., as well as additional sporting events throughout the year.
Pupils also work on their employability skills during their time in the Sixth Form. We have developed a pathways model which stimulates the pupils and enables them to work towards employability. The pathways model covers both the academic and vocational opportunities and qualifications that pupils work towards during their 3 years in the Sixth Form. We also offer pupils a series of work experience opportunities. Please see our vocational and employment section for more details.

\ About Behaviour Analysis
Behaviour Analysis
Therapies
Jargon Buster
Interdisciplinary Team
Behaviour analysis
Practice guided by behaviour analysis is a teaching approach that takes the scientific principles of learning and behaviour, and applies them in practice to teach important skills, personalised to an individual.
It can also be used to help reduce behaviours that challenge or that limit opportunities by teaching functional alternatives. Behaviour analysis helps us to understand how learning takes place, and how behaviour can be affected by the environment.
How we use behaviour analysis at BeyondAutism
At BeyondAutism, we use teaching strategies underpinned by behaviour analysis to teach our learners social, communication, academic and daily living skills tailored according to their specific needs. This forms part of our interdisciplinary approach with Speech and Language Therapists, Occupational Therapists and Teachers, to ensure a well-rounded, balanced curriculum for each of our learners that is focussed on their individual preferences and needs.
We use behaviour analysis to track progress and create positive, fun and motivating educational and learning experiences that make a real difference to our learners’ lives. Complex skills are broken down and taught step-by-step including daily living skills, communication, functional academic skills and social skills, to ultimately empower our learners to be as independent as possible, access their local communities and make informed choices about their ideal week.
Our teaching aims to:
Understand behaviour and why it occurs
Teach functional language and communication

Park House Mental Health & Wellbeing Vision Statement
We acknowledge that, whilst we all have unique perspectives, mental health and wellbeing is of central importance and intrinsic to all of our lives as staff, pupils, parents/carers.
The role of BeyondAutism Schools is to ensure that pupils are able to manage times of change and stress, and that they are supported and can access help when they need it.
We recognise that children and young adults' mental health is a crucial factor in their overall wellbeing and can affect their learning and achievement.
What good Mental Health and Wellbeing practices look like at Park House School
Why Park House School is working towards the Wellbeing Award Scheme
In September 2021 we started working towards the Wellbeing Award for Schools. We are delighted to have achieved the award in March 2023. More on the award can be found here.
"This reflects the impact that the school, staff, students and parents’ commitments to emotional wellbeing and good mental health has achieved across the school. I saw a wide range of good practice." Wellbeing Award report author Therese Hoyle.

How We Teach
“Leaders have developed an ambitious curriculum for pupils. It covers all the required areas of learning and gives pupils a broad, rich experience. Leaders have developed an education programme which is unique and tailored for each pupil.”
- Ofsted 2023
We use strategies underpinned by Behaviour Analysis in our teaching. Teaching with Behaviour Analysis helps us understand behaviours that challenge, ensuring our pupils access a broad, balanced and specialised curriculum - drawing on a range of assessment tools, the National Curriculum and working towards the outcomes stated on a pupil’s EHCP.
Our teaching focuses on language development, particularly functional communication. We aim to develop learning, independent living skills and personal, social and emotional development through highly effective teaching in a variety of ways.
Activities include outdoor playtime, art, music, PE, yoga, and swimming. Regular class community trips, library trips and other school and class outings are planned each term.
All pupils participate in weekly assemblies and there are drama opportunities throughout the year including a Song Club and a full length Winter Production in December. These opportunities improve communication and public speaking skills, boosting pupils’ confidence and self-esteem.
At Park House School we:
Break down skills into achievable goals
Generalise and maintain learned skills
“Staff ensure that pupils can use a variety of ways to communicate and express themselves confidently. They learn to use signing and visual cues, as well as verbal and written methods.”
- Ofsted 2023
